subject: [Polaris Analytics] Model upgrade caused latency spike & accuracy regressions
messages:
From: Elena Marquez <elena@polarisanalytics.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 19 Dec 2026 17:42:00 -0800
Subject: Urgent: large p99 spike + hallucinations since last night's model upgrade

Hi Ben / Marissa,

We pushed to prod around 02:20 UTC last night (your side told us model redwood-llm-v2.1 / quant profile int8-qp-1 was live) and since then we've seen: 
- p95 jumping from ~120ms to ~420ms; p99 to ~1.1s.
- 5xx error rate increased from ~0.7% to ~4.2% over the last 12 hours.
- A measurable uptick in incorrect entity linking / hallucinations in samples from our fraud-detection assistant (samples attached).

This is customer-facing and affecting our risk scoring pipelines. We've opened a ticket on our side but need immediate coordination. Can we get an incident bridge + a rollback plan?

I've attached a small bundle: p99_traces.csv (traces over the last 8 hours) and error-samples.jsonl (representative prompts + outputs).

Please advise on next steps — we need a mitigation window within the next 2 hours.

Thanks,
Elena
Lead Engineer, Polaris Analytics

Cc: Elena Marquez <elena@polarisanalytics.com>
Date: Sat, 19 Dec 2026 19:12:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Urgent: large p99 spike + hallucinations since last night's model upgrade

Quick triage notes (first 30m):
- We've reproduced the latency and error signals in our prod telemetry for Polaris' tenant. p99 for their hot path increased ~3x (180ms -> 520ms) starting at 02:17 UTC. Error rate (502/504) up ~3.5%.
- Correlated with a quant-profile switch event: int8-qp-1 was rolled to their dedicated pool as part of last night's optimization rollout. Kernel durations for the attention ops increased on A100 nodes for longer sequences; decode stalls observed.
- Also seeing a small but real regression in top-1 accuracy for key prompts used by their fraud assistant — outputs are more likely to drop entity context. Roughly +8% incorrect entity extractions in our sample set.

Attachments: quant-profile-diff.yaml (diff between currently live qp and previous qp-0.9), p99_traces.csv (extracted from their tenant ID).

Immediate mitigations I recommend: 
1) Traffic split to v2.0 non-quant variant for the hot path (can be done instantly with routing policy).
2) If customer agrees, rollback their dedicated pool to qp-0.9 (revert quant profile). That has the highest chance of fixing both latency & accuracy regressions.
3) Short-term scale-up: add 2 capacity nodes to their dedicated pool to reduce queueing while we test the above.

If we do steps 1+2 we should see p99 drop within a single quant-window (~10-15 minutes).

I'll prepare a short rollback playbook. Need Ben to confirm customer consent for plan + Lauren to authorize any billing/credit conversation. Vivek — can you validate the operational risk for immediate rollback?

Marissa
Director, Customer Reliability
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Marquez <elena@polarisanalytics.com>
Date: Sun, 20 Dec 2026 08:15:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Urgent: large p99 spike + hallucinations since last night's model upgrade

I ran a quick impact analysis. Technical notes:
- Root cause (probable): int8-qp-1 uses a new kernel path that reduces precision in KV-cache compression. For short prompts it's OK, but for their workload (longer context + large topK) it increases attention kernel durations and memory pressure which leads to stalls + queueing under their concurrency distribution.
- Risk of rollback: low. Reverting to qp-0.9 is a tested path on their Dedicated cluster; we expect no model weights change, just quant params. Time to revert ~6-10 minutes, plus ~10-15m stabilization.
- Short-term capacity bump: adding 2 x p4d-equivalent nodes will reduce the hot-path queueing; provisioning and warmup ~12 minutes. Cost note: this will increase spend for the environment by ~18% during the window.

Plan (proposed immediate actions):
A) Approve rollback to qp-0.9 for Polaris' dedicated pool (Vivek to execute).
B) Simultaneously provision + attach 2 nodes to Polaris pool (Vivek ops).
C) Route 20% of traffic to v2.0 non-quant variant as a safety net while we observe.

I'll file SUP-8921 and start the runbook. If Ben gets Polaris approval I'll execute step A and B now.

Vivek
Head of Production Systems
vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai

Related: https://jira.redwood.ai/SUP-8921

Date: Sun, 20 Dec 2026 13:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Polaris incident — immediate remediation plan & exec call at 11:00 PT

Elena / Adam —

Thank you for raising this. I'm very sorry for the customer impact. We own this. Summary and actions: 
- Issue: latency (p99) and error rate spike, plus measurable accuracy regressions correlated with last night's deployment of redwood-llm-v2.1 + int8-qp-1 to your dedicated pool.
- Immediate actions (starting now):
  1) We will rollback Polaris' quant profile to qp-0.9 (Vivek to execute). Expected stabilization 15-25 minutes.
  2) Add 2 capacity nodes to your dedicated pool to relieve queueing (Vivek executing in parallel).
  3) Route a safety 20% of traffic to v2.0 non-quant variant; this gives us a safe path if rollback shows any edge cases.
- Next steps: postmortem within 48 hours, compensatory credit for the incident (Lauren will coordinate), and a joint runbook review to prevent similar regressions during quant rollouts.

We're convening an exec bridge at 11:00 AM PT (invite sent). Please join if you can — we'll present telemetry, the rollback, and remediation timeline.

Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
